task_objective: Develop a risk-informed method for reducing security-control friction and monitoring consequences of redesigned controls.

rius.description: Identify actual friction points and the workarounds they prompt using user feedback, observed workflows, incident evidence or an equivalent source.

scoring_rule.1: Identify actual friction points and the workarounds they prompt using user feedback, observed workflows, incident evidence or an equivalent source.

rius.rationale: Grounds redesign in observed problems; no specific collection technique is compulsory.

rius.description: Assess the security risk of workarounds in the affected work or asset context, using justified likelihood/consequence reasoning or an equivalent qualitative or quantitative assessment rather than inconvenience alone.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Assess the security risk of workarounds in the affected work or asset context, using justified likelihood/consequence reasoning or an equivalent qualitative or quantitative assessment rather than inconvenience alone.

rius.rationale: Supplies the requested risk assessment without imposing a formula, mandatory numeric estimates or invented risk values.

rius.description: Explain how a lower-friction control or approved workflow addresses an identified friction point while retaining protection against the relevant security risk.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Explain how a lower-friction control or approved workflow addresses an identified friction point while retaining protection against the relevant security risk.
scoring_rule.0.5: Proposes a concrete lower-friction control or workflow for an identified friction point, but does not explain how it retains the relevant security protection; an explicitly unsafe removal of necessary protection scores 0.

rius.rationale: Simply relaxing controls can reproduce the risky workaround exposure; the central redesign must connect usability and protection.

rius.description: Specify how to observe unintended effects of the redesign, such as new workarounds, security incidents or displaced workflow problems, using follow-up feedback, monitoring or another concrete observation method.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Specify how to observe unintended effects of the redesign, such as new workarounds, security incidents or displaced workflow problems, using follow-up feedback, monitoring or another concrete observation method.

rius.rationale: Retains the requested follow-up phase without assuming that the redesign succeeds or prescribing a specific metric suite.
